title: The Equinox Cabin Opening
skyStory: The autumn equinox arrives before dawn, and the moon, now in Cancer and just under half lit, celebrates by redecorating the whole sky as a cozy living room. Throw blankets on the Milky Way. A lamp lit beside Orion. Cancer is ruled by the moon herself, so tonight she is home, slippers on, kettle whistling. Saturn brought the good biscuits.

reading: Day and night are equal this morning, and the cabin is officially open for the dark half of the year. Light the stove, or a candle, or just the warm lamp in the corner. Something in you settles when the season turns. The Tiger knows it is time to stretch out by the fire after a long, bright summer of running.

Cancer moons are about home, and home is not always a place. It might be a voice on the phone, a familiar mug, a friend who knows your stories already. Reach out to one of those homes today. The [[Four of Wands]] has strung garlands over the doorway and is waiting for you to walk through.
joel.mission: Light a candle or lamp at sundown on the equinox and say one sentence welcoming the dark half of the year.
joel.omen: Smoke rising straight up from a chimney. The new season is beginning on calm footing.

reading: From today, the nights grow longer, and every one of them carries you closer to your own solstice in December. The Mountain feels that shift in its bones like a homecoming in slow motion. The light is not leaving. It is going home to be born again on your birthday.

The shore at the equinox has a particular light, flat and silver, a horizon cut clean with a knife. If you can, stand somewhere you can see a long view and notice how balanced it looks. Your Life Path 11 likes these thresholds. Make a quiet wish for the dark months, something small and warm.
nancy.mission: Find a spot with a long view today, water or field or sky, and make one quiet wish for the coming dark season.
nancy.omen: A flock of geese heading south in a perfect V. The way forward is clear and shared.

together.text: Equinox day. Each of you name one cozy ritual for the dark half of the year, a Sunday soup, a reading chair, a nightly walk. Promise to report on it at the solstice. The moon is home tonight, and she wants you home too.
